tweets.text: RT @sethlazar: I've realised lately that I no longer think that the worst-case outcomes from powerful AI are *that* unlikely. I mean, they're still unlikely, but definitely important to attend to. So I've been wondering why I don't personally work on that aspect of AI governance much. I think it's because it's mostly a political problem now. Remaining disagreement over goals is unlikely to be resolved by a clever argument; governance means aren't my speciality; and others are better than me at motivating action too. OTOH *AGI alignment*, as a technical project, remains a fascinating area for philosophical engagement, and that's partly (though not entirely) motivated by avoiding existential risk. And then there's a vast array of questions opened up by the possibility (in my view likelihood) that we navigate the transition to powerful AI without humanity being wiped out.
